question: How long does the postnatal period typically last?
explanation: The postnatal period, or puerperium, is traditionally defined as the first six weeks following childbirth. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h1)

question: Why is the first few weeks after birth a critical time to watch new mothers closely?

options.A: Severe complications like heavy bleeding and infections happen most often then
options.B: Hormone levels drop to zero immediately after birth
options.C: Babies cry constantly during the first few days
options.D: Mothers are usually discharged before labor pain stops completely

explanation: You've got this! Life-threatening emergencies such as heavy bleeding (hemorrhage) and infections are most common right after delivery, which is why close nursing monitoring is so essential. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h1)

question: What do we call the wonderful process where the uterus shrinks back to its normal pre-pregnant size?
explanation: Great job thinking about postpartum anatomy! Involution is simply the medical word for the uterus gradually shrinking and recovering back to its normal state. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h2)

question: If a mother is still passing bright red lochia rubra on her fifth day postpartum, what might this mean?

options.A: The expected start of the mother's normal menstrual cycle
options.B: Normal progression of postpartum vaginal discharge
options.C: A potential delay or complication in normal uterine healing
options.D: Complete closure of the internal cervical os

explanation: Normally, bright red discharge only lasts for the first couple of days before turning brownish or pink. Seeing bright red blood on day five is a red flag that healing might be delayed or some tissue was retained. You're learning fast! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h2)

question: How often should you check vital signs during the first two hours after delivery?
explanation: Spot on! Checking vitals every fifteen minutes right after delivery helps us catch sudden bleeding or shock super early, keeping our patients safe. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h3)

question: You check a new mother and notice her uterus feels soft and is pushed over to the right side. What should you do first?

options.A: Assist the patient to empty her bladder
options.B: Massage the calves to prevent clots
options.D: Encourage heavy ambulation around the ward

explanation: A full bladder acts like a bully, pushing the uterus upward and to the side and stopping it from contracting properly. Helping her pee often fixes the problem instantly! Great nursing intuition. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h3)

question: What is the name of the first nutrient-rich, antibody-packed milk a mother produces after birth?
explanation: Colostrum is liquid gold for the newborn! It is packed with antibodies to protect the baby before the regular milk comes in. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h4)

question: Why is teaching a mother the correct way for her baby to latch crucial during breastfeeding?

options.A: It guarantees the infant will sleep through the night
options.B: It stops the baby from spitting up any milk
options.C: It prevents maternal nipple pain and ensures effective milk transfer
options.D: It forces the mother's milk to change from colostrum instantly

explanation: A good latch is a win-win: it keeps the mother's nipples safe from painful cracks and helps the baby get a full tummy efficiently! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h4)

question: Which of these is a classic sign of postpartum endometritis (infection of the uterus lining)?

options.A: Sudden weight gain and facial swelling
options.C: High blood pressure and visual changes

explanation: When the uterine lining gets infected, it usually lets you know through fever, tenderness, and vaginal discharge that smells unusual or foul. You're building great clinical instincts! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h5)

question: A new mother complains that her left calf is severely painful, swollen, and warm to the touch. What should you suspect first?
explanation: Warmth, swelling, and pain in just one leg are classic textbook signs of a deep vein thrombosis (DVT)—a blood clot that needs immediate medical attention. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h5)

question: What is a major difference between normal postpartum blues and postpartum depression?

options.A: Postpartum blues resolve on their own within two weeks
options.B: Postpartum depression appears on the first day after delivery
options.C: Postpartum depression only affects women who had cesarean births
options.D: Postpartum depression require immediate psychiatric admission

explanation: The 'baby blues' are mild and usually fade away within a couple of weeks without special treatment, whereas postpartum depression is heavier, lasts longer, and needs real support. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal symptom of the postpartum blues?

options.A: Temporary fatigue from broken sleep patterns
options.B: Mild mood swings and unexpected crying spells
options.C: Severe delusions and thoughts of harming the infant
options.D: Feeling slightly overwhelmed by new responsibilities

explanation: Crying spells and feeling overwhelmed are totally normal as hormones shift. However, delusions or thoughts of hurting the baby are never normal blues—they are signs of a severe emergency like postpartum psychosis. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h6)

question: Why do we encourage new mothers to get up and walk around (ambulate) early after childbirth?

options.A: To speed up the immediate closure of the cervix
options.B: To reduce the risk of blood clots and improve circulation
options.C: To encourage the baby to sleep through the night
options.D: To prevent the mother from producing too much colostrum

explanation: Getting moving gets the blood pumping! It keeps circulation strong and stops blood from pooling in the legs, preventing dangerous clots. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h7)

question: Why must nurses always teach postpartum women to clean their perineal area from front to back?

options.A: To stimulate faster contraction of the abdominal wall muscles
options.B: To ensure that lochia stops flowing within the first twenty-four hours
options.C: To prevent spreading bacteria from the anal region into the vagina or wound
options.D: To prevent painful swelling of the lower extremities

explanation: Wiping front to back keeps unwanted germs from the back passage away from healing tears or surgical stitches, preventing nasty infections! Simple hygiene makes a massive difference. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h7)

question: Which type of family planning method is generally considered safest for a breastfeeding mother in the early weeks?
explanation: Progestin-only options (like mini-pills or certain injectables) won't mess with her breastmilk supply, making them a great choice for nursing mums. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h8)

question: Why do we usually avoid combined estrogen-progestin contraceptives right after childbirth?

options.A: They prevent the uterus from completing normal involution
options.B: They can decrease milk supply and increase blood clot risk
options.C: They cause permanent infertility in nursing mothers

explanation: Estrogen can dry up breastmilk production and add to the already high risk of dangerous blood clots that new mothers face. Smart nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h8)

question: When is the standard comprehensive postnatal check usually scheduled after the initial hospital stay?
explanation: The six-week postnatal visit is the big milestone where we check that both the mother's body and mind have fully recovered from pregnancy and birth. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h9)

question: As a nurse preparing a mother for discharge, what is one of your most important responsibilities?

options.A: Ensuring the mother can name critical danger signs for herself and the baby
options.B: Confirming that lochia has completely stopped entirely
options.C: Scheduling permanent sterilization procedures before she leaves
options.D: Providing enough formula for the first three months of life

explanation: Before anyone goes home, we must make sure they know the warning signs to watch for so they can run back to the hospital if something goes wrong. Excellent safety practice! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h9)
